```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "A's payer is better established. Creators already pay a sourced percentage of their revenue (Patreon at 10% plus processing, Memberful at $49/mo plus 4.9%), so a fee-based product has a real money flow to attach to. B's payer is individual readers at a $5/mo anchor, and B's own case against cites structurally declining paid local-news behavior.",
    "A's demand evidence speaks directly to switching. Both sourced r/patreon quotes show creators actively looking to leave over fees. B's demand evidence is letters to editors about print papers in general (dating from 2008, 2017 and 2022). Those letters complain about cost and format, not about wanting a configurable edition.",
    "A has a sourced precedent of a small team reaching about $140K MRR. It is a single case and depends on an owned audience, but B has no comparable monetization precedent. B's closest validation is free open-source hobby clones, which hurt willingness to pay as much as they show demand.",
    "Each idea carries one major legal risk, and B's is harder to contain. A's compliance load (KYC, money transmission, 1099-K) can be reduced with a direct-Stripe-account model and a one-time attorney consult. B's core mechanic of scraping and AI-rewriting third-party news sits inside active copyright litigation, and the brief offers no mitigation.",
    "B's direct competitor and its free clones target the exact same single-reader use case. B also flags local feed scarcity as the hardest unsolved part, which leaves a solo founder little to differentiate on within 90 days."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's demand evidence is three newspaper reader letters, one from 2008. They complain about paying for unwanted sections or poor format, but none shows anyone willing to pay for a personalized or lighter edition. B's figure that only about 9% of Americans pay for local news is 'Pew-cited' with no link, so it counts as unsourced. The publisher-licensing payer is explicitly unvalidated.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate-to-low confidence. Both ideas sit in crowded markets with free or cheaper incumbents. A's only success case relied on a pre-existing niche audience, and its Reddit demand quotes show creators moving to Ko-fi rather than to a new entrant. A's main SEO channel is also acknowledged to be dominated by incumbents. A wins mainly because its payer and its switching intent are more directly evidenced, not because it shows a clear path to a first paying customer in 90 days."
}
```
